MOTHER ROAD RUN00:00

The Mother
Road Run

Somebody hid a prize at the far west end of Oklahoma's Route 66 and left a trail of locked boxes to get you there.

You start in the east, at Catoosa. Four stops, four lockboxes, four combinations. Crack one and it tells you where to drive next.

Three scout teams went out ahead of you and wrote down everything they could find. Their notes are on your table. That is all the help you get.

Drive west. Don't dawdle — somebody else is on the road too.

Stop 1 of 4 — Catoosa

The Blue Whale

Eighty feet of smiling concrete whale, half in a green pond, wearing a little hat. A zookeeper named Hugh Davis built it for his wife and it has been grinning at the highway ever since.

The lockbox is bolted inside the whale's mouth, at the top of the slide. Four digits.

▶ The combination

Hugh didn't build the whale alone, and neither of them hurried.

  • His friend Harold welded the iron skeleton. Find how many hours that took.
  • Hugh mixed and spread the concrete himself, one five-gallon bucket at a time. Find how many hours that took.

Add the two numbers together. That is the combination.

★ The box swings open!

Inside is a curled photograph of a giant golden man in a hard hat, and a note: "Keep west on 66 into Tulsa. He's standing at the fairgrounds. You can't miss him — he's the colour of cheap mustard and he is not subtle."

Stop 2 of 4 — Tulsa

The Golden Driller

He is enormous and slightly unsettling, one gloved hand resting on a real oil derrick, TULSA stamped across a belt buckle the size of a car door.

Someone has wired four small plaques to the fence around his boots. The lockbox hangs under the last one. It takes a word.

▶ The combination

Four plaques are bolted to the fence. Three of them have their facts right. One of them does not.

He weighs 43,500 pounds.
He was first built for a petroleum exposition in 1953.
The real oil derrick under his hand was hauled in from Ponca City.
The Oklahoma legislature made him the state monument in 1979.

Work out which plaque has it wrong. Then find out what it should have said. The combination is that one word.

This dial takes a word, not a number.

★ The latch pops!

A bottle cap falls out, and a torn napkin: "Southwest out of Tulsa, past Chandler, past the round barn. Stop where the sixty-six-foot pop bottle is. Arcadia."

Stop 3 of 4 — Arcadia

Pops 66

A steel soda bottle sixty-six feet tall stands out front, throwing colored light across the parking lot, and behind the glass are seven hundred kinds of pop shelved in a rainbow.

The lockbox is tucked between the orange sodas and the red ones. Five digits.

▶ The combination

Five dusty bottles stand on the shelf above the box. Somebody has numbered the shelf underneath them, 1 through 5, left to right, and stuck a handwritten label on each bottle where the flavor should be.

Bottle 1 — the year Pops opened here in Arcadia
Bottle 2 — the year Route 66 was commissioned
Bottle 3 — the year the Tower Theatre opened in Oklahoma City
Bottle 4 — the year the round barn was built up the road
Bottle 5 — the year Route 66 was decommissioned

Work out all five years. Then put the bottles in order oldest to newest and read off their shelf numbers in that new order.

For example — if there were only two bottles, and bottle 1 turned out to be 1975 while bottle 2 turned out to be 1940, the older one goes first, so the answer would be 21.

★ It opens with a hiss!

Inside, a ticket stub for a movie that played in 1952, and a note: "Keep west into the city. Northwest 23rd Street was Route 66 once. Find the neon that spells TOWER."

Stop 4 of 4 — Oklahoma City

Tower Theatre

The blade sign juts out over the sidewalk on Uptown 23rd, five porcelain letters stacked down its side, humming. This street was Route 66 before the interstate took the traffic away.

The last lockbox is in the ticket booth, under the counter. Four digits, and this one wants everywhere you've been.

▶ The combination

Four years, one from each stop on this run.

  1. The year Hugh Davis finished the whale at Catoosa.
  2. The year the Golden Driller took his permanent place at the fairgrounds.
  3. The year Pops opened in Arcadia.
  4. The year the Tower Theatre first opened its doors.

Add the first three together. Subtract the fourth. That is the combination.

★ The drawer slides out!

No prize. Just a postcard of a thirty-foot silver astronaut standing on a street corner, and six words on the back: "Weatherford. Broadway and Main. Come collect."

Weatherford — Space City of Oklahoma

You Made It!

Thirty feet of silver astronaut looks down at you without a face. Four hundred miles of Mother Road behind you, four boxes cracked, and here he is, waiting.

AND THE PRIZE IS…
THE FRIENDS YOU
MADE ALONG THE WAY!

00:00
